decoy_bugs.summary: Unsigned integers above i64::MAX (u64, usize, u128) are converted to Lua by a wrapping cast, so u64::MAX arrives in Lua as the integer -1 instead of a float.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: When an unsigned Rust integer greater than i64::MAX goes to Lua, whether through IntoLua::into_lua, a function-call argument, or Table::set, Lua gets a negative Value::Integer (math.type 'integer', x < 0) instead of a positive float.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: IntoLua::into_lua and push_into_stack in the lua_convert_int! macro (src/conversion.rs:811 and :818), called with a u64/usize/u128 value v where v > i64::MAX as u64.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran a probe under tmp/p/crate/tests/probe.rs with ./run cargo test --features lua54,vendored,serde,macros --test probe. u64::MAX.into_lua gave Number(18446744073709552000), (i64::MAX+1).into_lua gave Number(9223372036854776000), and u128::MAX gave a Number. Passing u64::MAX and usize::MAX as function arguments gave math.type == 'float' with x = 1.8446744073709552e19, and globals().set("g", u64::MAX) gave 'float false' for math.type(g) and g < 0. cast() returns None, so the code falls back to lua_Number and never wraps.

decoy_bugs.summary: String::to_str only checks UTF-8 up to the first embedded NUL byte, so a Lua string like "ok\0\xff" is returned as a &str holding invalid UTF-8.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: When a Lua string contains a NUL byte followed by bytes that are not valid UTF-8, String::to_str, and the FromLua for StdString built on it, return Ok with a str whose bytes after the NUL are invalid UTF-8.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: BorrowedStr::try_from (src/string.rs:309) validating the slice from String::to_slice (src/string.rs:118, lua_tolstring at :132) on a string that contains an interior NUL.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe through ./run. lua.create_string(b"ab\0\xff").to_str() and a script-made "ok\0\255\254" both returned Err(FromLuaConversionError { message: "invalid utf-8 sequence of 1 bytes from index 3" }), and eval::<String> of "ok\0\255" returned the same error. A valid "a\0b" returned Ok("a\0b") with as_bytes().len() == 3. lua_tolstring reports the full length, and str::from_utf8 checks the whole slice.

false_findings.text:
**Fixed-size array conversion silently truncates longer tables**
src/conversion.rs:954 (from_lua).
Converting a Lua table with more than N sequence elements to [T; N] succeeds and returns only the first N elements, so a script sending {1,2,3} to a parameter of type [i32; 2] gets [1, 2] with no error.
The impl collects sequence_values() into a Vec and turns it into an array without comparing the table length to N first.
Running lua.load("return {1,2,3}").eval::<[i32; 2]>() in a test returned Ok([1, 2]).
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe through ./run. eval::<[i32; 2]>() on {1,2,3} returned Err(FromLuaConversionError { to: "[i32; 2]", message: "expected table of length 2, got 3" }), and [i32; 3] from a 5-element table also returned Err. Only an exact-length table returned Ok([1, 2, 3]). vec.try_into() at conversion.rs:970 fails on any length mismatch.

false_findings.text:
**char conversion panics on surrogate code points**
src/conversion.rs:756 (from_lua).
A script that passes an integer in the surrogate range (0xD800 to 0xDFFF) to a Rust callback taking char panics inside the callback, instead of getting a conversion error.
The integer goes through cast() and then char::from_u32, whose result is unwrapped without a check for surrogates.
Calling a create_function(|_, c: char| ...) callback from Lua as f(0xD800) panicked with a 'called Option::unwrap() on a None value' message.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe through ./run. eval::<char>() on 0xD800, 0xDFFF, 0x110000, -1, 0x100000041 and math.mininteger all returned Err("error converting Lua integer to char (integer out of range when converting to char)"). The callback f(0xD800) returned a 'bad argument #1' Lua error and did not panic. The code uses .and_then(char::from_u32).ok_or_else(...) at conversion.rs:760-766, with no unwrap.

false_findings.text:
**Table::is_empty leaks a ref-thread slot on every call**
src/table.rs:463 (is_empty).
Each call to is_empty on an empty table leaves the pushed nil key on the internal ref thread, so calling it in a loop grows that thread's stack without bound until Lua runs out of stack.
The function pushes nil and calls lua_next on the ref thread, but only pops in the non-empty branch, and returns true early without restoring the stack top.
A loop of 3,000,000 is_empty() calls on an empty table made lua.used_memory() grow steadily and then failed with a stack overflow on the next create_table.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe through ./run. Called is_empty() 3,000,000 times on each of an empty table, a sequence and a hash table. Every result was correct, used_memory went from 23808 before to 22683 after gc_collect, and a create_table/set/get afterwards returned Ok("x"). lua_next pops the key itself when it returns 0, so the early-return path leaves the stack balanced. The other path pops key and value with lua_pop(ref_thread, 2).

false_findings.text:
**as_bytes_with_nul reads one byte past the Lua string buffer**
src/string.rs:113 (as_bytes_with_nul).
For strings whose length fills their allocation exactly, such as the empty string or interned short strings, the returned slice ends with a byte outside the string data. The last byte is then unspecified memory instead of 0.
The unsafe block builds a slice of len() + 1 from the as_bytes pointer, assuming every Lua string has a terminating NUL, without checking that the byte exists.
In a test, lua.create_string(b"").as_bytes_with_nul() and a 64-byte string gave a last byte that changed from run to run and was not always 0.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe through ./run. as_bytes_with_nul() on "", "a", "a\0b", a 64-byte string and a 100000-byte string.rep result always had length len+1 and last byte Some(0). Lua always allocates and writes the '\0' terminator after the string contents, both short and long, so the extra byte is inside the object and always 0.

false_findings.text:
**Large Variadic returns overrun the Lua stack**
src/multi.rs:301 (push_into_stack_multi).
A Rust callback that returns a Variadic with hundreds of thousands of values writes past the end of the Lua stack, which corrupts memory or crashes, instead of returning an error.
The function checks the stack only once, for nresults + 1 slots computed with self.len() as i32, then pushes every value in a loop with no further check.
Returning Variadic::from((0..500_000).collect::<Vec<i64>>()) from a create_function callback and evaluating select('#', f(500000)) crashed the test process with SIGSEGV.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Ran the probe through ./run. select('#', f(n)) returned Ok(100000), Ok(500000) and Ok(990000). table.pack(f(200000)) returned (200000, 199999). n = 2,000,000 returned a clean Lua error, 'out of Lua stack, too many arguments to a Lua function or too many return values from a callback', with no crash. check_stack grows the stack to nresults+1 before any push, or returns Err when that is past the limit.
